 Cason Wallace will undergo surgery to to repair a left labrum tear.
 Wallace had already been ruled out for Monday’s game following an early exit on Sunday, but it now appears the injury is going to keep him sidelined a while longer. The hits just keep coming for OKC, with Jalen Williams (leg) set to have surgery as well. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain will both take on significant roles until Wallace and/or Williams return.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Related Player News
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 The Thunder have three new starters for Monday’s game, and two (McCain and Mitchell) could hold onto those roles for the foreseeable future. Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) could miss the rest of the season due to injuries that require surgery. “Kenny Hustle” starts for Chet Holmgren, who is dealing with right patellar tendinitis. 
 Jalen Williams 
 OKC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #8 
 Jalen Williams has suffered a fractured fibula and a dislocated ankle. 
 Williams’s injury was gruesome, and this diagnosis confirms it. General manager Sam Presti said a timeline will be provided following the surgery, but at this time, it’s unclear exactly how long he’ll be out. However, given the severity, it’s safe to say it will be a lengthy absence for him. Jared McCain and Ajay Mitchell should both take on larger roles with Cason Wallace (shoulder) set to undergo surgery as well. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Cason Wallace (shoulder) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Wallace left Sunday’s game with a shoulder injury and didn’t return. He’ll subsequently miss Monday’s game against the Bucks. Ajay Mitchell is certainly a candidate for more minutes and potentially a starting spot with Wallace sidelined. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell accounted for 18 points (8-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Clippers. 
 The Thunder lost Cason Wallace (shoulder) in the first quarter on Sunday. While Mitchell wasn’t the choice to start the third quarter, his role will expand if Wallace misses time. Jared McCain (three points, one rebound, one steal, and one three-pointer) replaced Wallace, and he can provide points and three-pointers in that role. However, Mitchell is the better option for fantasy managers left choosing between the two on the waiver wire. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Cason Wallace (shoulder) will not return vs. Clippers. 
 Wallace headed to the locker late in the first quarter after running into an Isaiah Jackson screen. This is something for fantasy managers to monitor as the Thunder play the Suns on Monday. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell amassed 12 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five steals and one blocked shot in Thursday’s win over the Nuggets. 
 While he may not be in the Thunder’s starting lineup, Mitchell can still provide solid fantasy value. He played 24 minutes against the Nuggets, doubling his point total from Tuesday’s win over the Spurs. More important for fantasy managers were the “stocks": Mitchell tallied six steals and blocks after recording none in San Antonio. Five-steal nights are unlikely to be the norm, but Mitchell can be close to a top-100 fantasy player for a second consecutive season. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Thunder and Cason Wallace agreed to a five-year, $139 million extension. 
 Wallace and the Thunder had until Monday at 6 PM Eastern to agree to a rookie-scale extension, and they got it done on Sunday night. With the Thunder trading Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe, and Aaron Wiggins during the offseason, Wallace moves into a full-time starting role. He was close to a top-100 player in category leagues last season, and that may represent Wallace’s floor in 2026-27. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell posted three points (1-of-5 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and one blocked shot in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 On a night when three of Oklahoma City’s five projected starters were available, Mitchell came off the bench. Cason Wallace, the replacement in the starting lineup on most nights last season, started against the Bucks and appears likely to keep that role. However, this doesn’t mean fantasy managers considering Mitchell should panic. He showed last season that he can provide consistent category league value in a reserve role, and that shouldn’t change in 2026-27, especially with his playing time expected to increase. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Cason Wallace accounted for seven points (2-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 Like Oklahoma City’s other projected starters, Wallace sat out the team’s preseason opener on Tuesday. He logged 18 minutes on Wednesday, dishing out six assists without committing a turnover. Wallace didn’t have a great night shooting the ball, but he did a little bit of everything else. He was the fifth starter on most nights last season when Oklahoma City was down a man, and it appears Wallace will be a full-time starter following the trade of Luguentz Dort. That makes him a more appealing option within the first 100 picks in standard drafts. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Thunder general manager Sam Presti names Cason Wallace, Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain as players that will play more minutes this season. 
 Not only will all three take on larger roles with Luguentz Dort now in Atlanta, but Presti is expecting genuine jumps in their production. All 3 players had strong stretches for OKC last season, and they’ll be relied on once again to help the Thunder get back on track after losing in the Western Conference Finals last season. Wallace seems like the most likely choice to start, but Mitchell and McCain will play big minutes off the bench.

 It has been a relatively quiet start to the season for Diabaté, but he was able to showcase just how good he is as a rebounder in this one.  Naz Reid posted a double-double on Monday with 18 points (8-of-22 FGs), 12 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers against the Wizards.
 It was a rough start to this game for Reid, and he had just two points on 1-of-3 FGs through three quarters. However, he was incredibly aggressive in the fourth quarter, and it paid off. He had 16 points and seven rebounds in just the fourth quarter, which allowed Charlotte to hang on to the win despite a big fourth quarter from Washington. Reid has gotten off to a strong start to the year for Charlotte and should continue to be a big part of their offense.

 Joan Beringer finished Monday’s loss to the Cavaliers with 12 points (6-of-6 FGs), seven rebounds and two blocked shots.
 On a night when starting center Rudy Gobert (five points, 19 rebounds, two assists and one block) shot 0-of-8 from the field, Beringer stepped up with the fifth double-digit scoring night of his young NBA career. He was perfect from the field while also providing solid rebounding and shot-blocking. Beringer still isn’t at the point where he should be rostered in redraft leagues, but his long-term outlook is good.

 Meleek Thomas tallied 16 points (6-of-10 FGs), two rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Timberwolves.
 After sitting out Cleveland’s first two games, Thomas checked into Monday’s contest with 5:53 left in the first quarter. The rookie wing wasn’t bashful, shooting 3-of-5 from the field and scoring eight points in the period. Thomas’ 16 points were the third-most on the team, behind Donovan Mitchell and James Harden. While he did most of his damage in two categories, points and three-pointers, Thomas may have done enough to stick in the rotation.

 Caleb Wilson recorded 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Monday’s matchup was tough for Wilson, as the Celtics rolled out a lineup led by Jayson Tatum and Paul George. However, the rookie forward finished Monday’s defeat 6-of-10 from two and managed to do a little bit of everything in his 32 minutes on the floor. The Bulls may be 1-3, but Wilson’s start to the season has been encouraging overall.

 Norman Powell tallied 20 points (5-of-11 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), one rebound, two assists, four steals and four three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Celtics.
 Powell’s shot fell at a higher rate than it did during the opening week, with the veteran guard shooting 34.1 percent from the field in Chicago’s first three games. A bonus for fantasy managers was four steals, bringing Powell’s total to 10 over four games. He’s averaged at least one steal per game each of the last two seasons, so Powell managers may get a little more value in that category.

 Josh Giddey finished Monday’s loss to the Celtics with 11 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, four assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.
 After shooting a combined 7-of-26 from the field in Chicago’s first three games, Giddey was more accurate on Monday. Unfortunately for him and the Bulls, that didn’t keep them from getting blown out in Boston. Overall, Giddey’s final stat line wasn’t great, but those rostering him can’t ignore that he shot better than in Week 1.

 Brandon Miller

 Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 39 points (15-of-28 FGs), six rebounds, one assist, three steals, two blocks and five three-pointers in a 110-103 win over the Wizards on Monday.
 The volume has been there all season, but the shots finally started falling for Miller in this game. That allowed him to set a new career high for scoring and score at least 30 points for a second straight game. Until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Coby White (calf) return, Miller is going to see as many shots as he wants. He has taken 57 shots over Charlotte’s last two games and should continue to see an insane amount of usage on offense, with a trip to Detroit up next on the schedule on Wednesday.
